action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions targeting user goals (workflow enablement, pain points with SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter), acceptance criteria, and trade-off reasoning. Questions integrate 5W1H, Socratic method, and MoSCoW prioritization to decompose sklearn_2021q4 requirements and elicit actionable acceptance criteria for abstract class design.

Generated 12 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class design), pain points (groups parameter limitations), acceptance criteria (success definition), and workflow context (feature selection lifecycle) for sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement. Questions span motivation, alternatives, use cases, prioritization, and trade-offs aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 standards.

Generated 11 interview questions targeting user goals, pain points, and acceptance criteria for sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter enhancement. Questions employ 5W1H framework (What/Who/Why/When/Where/How), Socratic method for deep exploration, and MoSCoW prioritization alignment. Chain-of-Thought decomposition: (1) identify pain point, (2) map stakeholders, (3) probe root causes, (4) sequence workflow, (5) locate constraints, (6) define success, (7) ground in examples, (8) explore alternatives, (9) assess second-order effects, (10) verify architectural fit, (11) prioritize relative to portfolio.

End-user requires abstract feature selector base class with grouped cross-validation support in SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() to enable efficient, reusable feature selection across ML pipelines while preventing data leakage in stratified datasets.

End-user requirements for sklearn feature selection: (1) Abstract base class to eliminate cross-cutting concerns (validation, logging, CV) across selector implementations; (2) SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter for stratified CV on grouped/correlated features; (3) Enable time-series and hierarchical data workflows preventing data leakage while reducing development time by 40%.

End-user requirements center on reducing manual feature selection overhead (30-40% of dev time) through an abstract base class pattern for reusable selector logic, and enabling grouped/stratified feature selection in SequentialFeatureSelector to handle correlated features, domain constraints, and temporal dependencies without manual partitioning.

Clarifying the scope of the abstract base class pattern, the dual interpretation of 'groups' parameter (feature vs. sample groupings), primary optimization goal (automation vs. validation), group selection semantics (all-or-none vs. individual), ecosystem scope, performance constraints, and hierarchical group support to disambiguate the feature selection enhancement requirements.

EndUser raises 5 critical clarifications on ambiguous requirements: (1) scope of proposed abstract base class pattern, (2) semantic definition and conflict resolution for 'groups' parameter, (3) primary goal (automation vs. statistical rigor), (4) template method enforcement level, and (5) efficiency vs. correctness trade-offs for high-dimensional scenarios. These questions must be resolved before detailed design to prevent rework.

Six clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities: (1) abstract class scope (new ABC vs. mixin refactoring), (2) groups parameter semantics (feature groupings vs. sample groupings vs. both), (3) primary objective trade-off (automation vs. statistical rigor), (4) conflict resolution strategy for dual-purpose groups, (5) abstract class method signatures and backward compatibility, (6) measurable success criteria. Chain-of-thought identified that requirement conflates feature-level and sample-level grouping concerns, and lacks explicit prioritization between automation and validation objectives.

End user requirements partially confirmed: abstract base class needed for feature selector standardization; SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() must support grouped cross-validation. Requires refinement on scope of 'groups' parameter (sample-level vs. feature-level grouping) and inheritance design strategy (new ABC vs. reference implementation extraction). Primary goal confirmed as dual: reducing manual effort + improving statistical rigor for grouped feature dependencies.

End-user requirements validated: abstract base class (BaseFeatureSelector) and groups parameter for SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() are confirmed. Refined scope clarifies groups must support both sample-stratification (primary) and feature-grouping (secondary). Primary goal is reducing manual effort while improving statistical rigor through grouped cross-validation. Decision needed on feature-grouping implementation timeline.

EndUser confirms need for BaseFeatureSelector abstract class with standardized methods and validates SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() 'groups' parameter for sample-level stratification. Requirement is refined to support dual-mode groups (sample stratification primary, feature groupings secondary). Primary objective is reducing manual effort (30-40% time savings) while improving statistical rigor through proper handling of non-i.i.d. data and correlated feature clusters.

Consolidated 6 structured interview records from sklearn_2021q4 case addressing two interconnected requirements: (1) Abstract base class for feature selectors to standardize interface and eliminate duplication, and (2) Groups parameter for SequentialFeatureSelector supporting sample-level stratification (MUST) and optional feature-level groupings (SHOULD). Quantified pain point: 30-40% development time overhead in feature selection. All confirmations validated; dual-mode groups design requires implementation decision and API documentation. Records follow ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability and BABOK elicitation standards.

Six prioritized user requirements synthesized from sklearn feature selection interviews: (1-2) MUST deliver BaseFeatureSelector ABC and sample-level groups parameter for SequentialFeatureSelector to enable stratified cross-validation and eliminate code duplication; (3-4) SHOULD implement optional feature-level groupings with dual-mode design resolving sample vs. feature stratification trade-offs; (5) MUST maintain sklearn API compatibility; (6) COULD target 30-40% development time reduction. All items traced to interview records, enduser confirmations, and clarification dialogues per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148.

Chain-of-Thought Analysis: The Deployer role requires probing three dimensions: (1) Infrastructure capacity—CI/CD, test coverage, Python/dependency matrix—to assess whether dual-mode groups parameter and new ABC introduce release friction; (2) Security/API stability—type validation, conflict resolution between sample-level and feature-level groupings, error handling—to ensure robust sklearn integration; (3) Scalability expectations—maximum dataset/feature size, lazy evaluation needs, downstream integrations—to validate that the design supports the 30-40% development time reduction goal without creating performance or compatibility bottlenecks. These nine targeted questions decompose the requirements into deployment-facing constraints that will inform API design decisions and risk mitigation strategies.

Deployer interview targets eight critical dimensions: infrastructure constraints (deployment targets, resource limits), security mandates (audit trails, compliance), scalability expectations (runtime/memory targets, parallelization), backward compatibility (sklearn integration stability), ecosystem alignment (cross-validator compatibility), validation infrastructure (testing frameworks), production observability (monitoring/logging), and conflict resolution policies (dual-mode groups precedence). These probe whether BaseFeatureSelector and dual-mode groups design can satisfy operational, security, and performance requirements across sklearn's distributed ecosystem.

Formulated 8 targeted Deployer interview questions spanning infrastructure constraints (environments, scale, memory), security mandates (data governance, auditability), scalability expectations (1000+ features, performance overhead), backward compatibility (existing deployments), cross-validation integration (sklearn conventions), monitoring requirements (group metrics), conflict resolution (dual-mode priority), and extensibility scope (future selectors). Questions probe deployment-specific tradeoffs between sample-level stratification fidelity, feature-level grouping semantics, and sklearn API conformance.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for BaseFeatureSelector ABC and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(groups=) deployment across sklearn CI/CD pipeline (Python 3.8-3.10, multi-OS); mandates type/bounds validation for groups parameter to prevent data leakage; targets <5% scalability overhead for 1000+ features; enforces backward compatibility (groups=None default) and dual-mode design documentation (sample-level primary, feature-level optional); requires eager validation at fit() time and full integration with existing sklearn.model_selection cross-validation framework.

Deployer confirms infrastructure support for Python 3.8-3.10 across major OS platforms, enforces security validation of groups parameter (bounds-checking, type validation), targets <5% performance overhead for high-dimensional datasets (1000+ features), and operationalizes dual-mode groups parameter (sample-level stratification primary, feature-level grouping optional) integrated with sklearn cross-validation framework while maintaining backward compatibility and 95%+ test coverage.

Deployer confirms infrastructure support (Python 3.8-3.10, multi-platform CI/CD), enforces security validation of groups parameter (bounds-checking, type validation), targets <5% performance overhead for 1000+ feature datasets, and establishes operational procedures for dual-mode groups parameter (sample-level primary, feature-level optional) with backward-compatible ABC design reducing feature selection development time from 30-40% to <15% of pipeline effort.

Deployer raises 5 critical clarifications on groups parameter dual-mode design (conflict resolution, validation scope), BaseFeatureSelector ABC method signature compatibility with sklearn conventions, feature-level vs. sample-level grouping priority (Phase 1 vs. Phase 2), and backward compatibility strategy to resolve ambiguities blocking implementation and ensure scalability/security requirements are achievable within sklearn CI/CD constraints.

Seven clarifications raised by Deployer role addressing critical ambiguities in dual-mode groups parameter design, BaseFeatureSelector ABC method signature compatibility, conflict resolution semantics, security validation scope, and scalability constraints. All items directly impact infrastructure deployment, API compatibility, and performance targets (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 compliance).

Deployer raises six critical clarifications on groups parameter dual-mode semantics (conflict resolution, validation rules, selection atomicity), BaseFeatureSelector ABC method signature compatibility with **kwargs, backwards compatibility with existing SequentialFeatureSelector code, and explicit scope definition for sample-level vs feature-level grouping modes. These clarifications are prerequisite for infrastructure deployment planning and sklearn API compliance validation.

Deployer confirms BaseFeatureSelector ABC and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(groups=) are validated MUST requirements aligned with sklearn API conventions and infrastructure constraints. Dual-mode groups parameter (sample-level primary, feature-level future) requires explicit design decision to avoid API ambiguity. Security validation, scalability targets (<5% overhead), and CI/CD compatibility across Python 3.8-3.10 platforms are confirmed feasible. Recommend **kwargs support in BaseFeatureSelector.fit() and contiguous integer group indices per sklearn standards.

Deployer confirms BaseFeatureSelector ABC as MUST with sklearn API compliance and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(groups=None) sample-level stratification as MUST with <5% performance overhead. Resolves dual-mode conflict: sample-level groups PRIMARY (sklearn standard), feature-level grouping deferred as optional future extension. Validates security (type/bounds-checking), infrastructure (Python 3.8-3.10, numpy/scipy), and scalability (O(n_samples) memory, <5% overhead on 1000+ features). Refines fit() signature to support (X, y, groups=None, **kwargs) for forward compatibility.

Deployer role validates infrastructure compatibility (Python 3.8-3.10, multi-OS CI/CD), enforces security (groups parameter validation, bounds-checking), confirms scalability targets (<5% overhead), and resolves dual-mode conflict by prioritizing sample-level groups as primary mode with feature-level grouping deferred. Key refinements: finalize BaseFeatureSelector.fit() signature for forward compatibility, define exact groups parameter validation rules, and ensure backward compatibility with existing sklearn API.
